system.one_liner: A systematic study of four ways to supervise a vision-language-action model with image-based or action-based latent actions under one unified baseline.

content.variant_note: left panel fixes the shared VLA framework, right panel groups four sibling strategy schematics under two numbered perspectives
content.argues: Latent actions can supervise a VLA from two perspectives, regularizing the trajectory or unifying the target space, realised by four comparable integration strategies.
content.subject: A unified VLA framework, the latent-action machinery of two perspectives and four strategy schematics showing where latent actions attach to the VLM.

lessons.what_to_learn: Fix the shared framework in a left panel and stack the variants as aligned rows that share the same input box in a right panel; give each module one colour that never changes so only the changing target stands out, and group the rows under numbered perspective headings whose key terms are coloured like the boxes.
lessons.suits: Systematic studies comparing several ways to plug one extra supervision signal into a shared model, with a few shared components and several variants.

evidence: Left: a unified VLA pipeline; right: our two perspectives and four integration strategies.
(1) Regularizing the Trajectory, where we leverage imagebased latent actions to provide high-level visual plans
These perspectives form four distinct supervision strategies for the VLM.

summary: The paper studies how to supervise vision-language-action models with latent actions under one unified baseline. Figure 1 is a two-panel overview. The left dashed panel, VLA Framework, shows a pink LATENT ACTIONs card and a pale-yellow ACTIONs card above a VLM box, with three line-icon inputs below. The right panel, VLM Supervision, has two numbered perspectives: image-based latent actions, where two robot frames feed a Latent Action Model and a codebook of codes such as Move Right, Pick and Place, and action-based latent actions, where photos from several action spaces map into a VLM token space. Four aligned strategy schematics at the right edge show where latent actions attach to the V+L features, with one colour per module.
summary_zh: 论文在统一基线下比较用潜在动作监督 VLA 模型的方法。图一左侧是 VLA 框架，右侧分两种视角：基于图像的潜在动作（帧对、潜在动作模型、码本）与基于动作的潜在动作（多动作空间映射到词元空间），右缘并列四种策略。
notes: Prior side-by-side-contrast and model-anatomy kept; concept-schematic added for the codebook and token-space pictures. Panels are the two dashed frames; the four strategies are titled rows, not framed panels. No arrows are drawn inside the left panel, so the input and target roles of its cards come from layout only. The purple dashed Regulated Path is read from its label and shape.
